package org.decimal4j.immutable;

import java.math.BigDecimal;
import java.math.BigInteger;
import java.math.RoundingMode;

import org.decimal4j.api.Decimal;
import org.decimal4j.api.DecimalArithmetic;
import org.decimal4j.base.AbstractImmutableDecimal;
import org.decimal4j.exact.Multipliable14f;
import org.decimal4j.factory.Factory14f;
import org.decimal4j.mutable.MutableDecimal14f;
import org.decimal4j.scale.Scale14f;

/**
 * <tt>Decimal14f</tt> represents an immutable decimal number with a fixed
 * number of 14 digits to the right of the decimal point.
 * <p>
 * All methods for this class throw {@code NullPointerException} when passed a
 * {@code null} object reference for any input parameter.
 */
public final class Decimal14f extends AbstractImmutableDecimal<Scale14f, Decimal14f> {

	private static final long serialVersionUID = 1L;

	/** Scale value 14 for {@code Decimal14f} returned by {@link #getScale()}.*/
	public static final int SCALE = 14;

	/** Scale metrics constant for {@code Decimal14f} returned by {@link #getScaleMetrics()}.*/
	public static final Scale14f METRICS = Scale14f.INSTANCE;

	/** Factory constant for {@code Decimal14f} returned by {@link #getFactory()}.*/
	public static final Factory14f FACTORY = Factory14f.INSTANCE;
	
	/**
	 * Default arithmetic for {@code Decimal14f} performing unchecked operations with rounding mode 
	 * {@link RoundingMode#HALF_UP HALF_UP}.
	 */
	public static final DecimalArithmetic DEFAULT_ARITHMETIC = METRICS.getDefaultArithmetic();
	
	/**
	 * Default arithmetic for {@code Decimal14f} performing checked operations with rounding mode 
	 * {@link RoundingMode#HALF_UP HALF_UP}.
	 */
	public static final DecimalArithmetic DEFAULT_CHECKED_ARITHMETIC = METRICS.getDefaultCheckedArithmetic();

	/** The unscaled long value that represents one.*/
	public static final long ONE_UNSCALED = METRICS.getScaleFactor();

	/** The {@code Decimal14f} constant zero.*/
	public static final Decimal14f ZERO = new Decimal14f(0);
    /**
     * A constant holding the smallest positive value a {@code Decimal14f}
     * can have, 10<sup>-14</sup>.
     */
	public static final Decimal14f ULP = new Decimal14f(1);

    /**
     * Initialize static constant array when class is loaded.
     */
    private static final int MAX_CONSTANT = 10;
    private static final Decimal14f POS_CONST[] = new Decimal14f[MAX_CONSTANT+1];
    private static final Decimal14f NEG_CONST[] = new Decimal14f[MAX_CONSTANT+1];

    static {
        for (int i = 1; i <= MAX_CONSTANT; i++) {
            POS_CONST[i] = new Decimal14f(ONE_UNSCALED * i);
            NEG_CONST[i] = new Decimal14f(-ONE_UNSCALED * i);
        }
    }

	/** The {@code Decimal14f} constant 1.*/
	public static final Decimal14f ONE = valueOf(1);
	/** The {@code Decimal14f} constant 2.*/
	public static final Decimal14f TWO = valueOf(2);
	/** The {@code Decimal14f} constant 3.*/
	public static final Decimal14f THREE = valueOf(3);
	/** The {@code Decimal14f} constant 4.*/
	public static final Decimal14f FOUR = valueOf(4);
	/** The {@code Decimal14f} constant 5.*/
	public static final Decimal14f FIVE = valueOf(5);
	/** The {@code Decimal14f} constant 6.*/
	public static final Decimal14f SIX = valueOf(6);
	/** The {@code Decimal14f} constant 7.*/
	public static final Decimal14f SEVEN = valueOf(7);
	/** The {@code Decimal14f} constant 8.*/
	public static final Decimal14f EIGHT = valueOf(8);
	/** The {@code Decimal14f} constant 9.*/
	public static final Decimal14f NINE = valueOf(9);
	/** The {@code Decimal14f} constant 10.*/
	public static final Decimal14f TEN = valueOf(10);
	/** The {@code Decimal14f} constant 100.*/
	public static final Decimal14f HUNDRED = new Decimal14f(100 * ONE_UNSCALED);
	/** The {@code Decimal14f} constant 1000.*/
	public static final Decimal14f THOUSAND = new Decimal14f(1000 * ONE_UNSCALED);

	/** The {@code Decimal14f} constant -1.*/
	public static final Decimal14f MINUS_ONE = valueOf(-1);

	/** The {@code Decimal14f} constant 0.5.*/
	public static final Decimal14f HALF = new Decimal14f(ONE_UNSCALED / 2);
	/** The {@code Decimal14f} constant 0.1.*/
	public static final Decimal14f TENTH = new Decimal14f(ONE_UNSCALED / 10);
	/** The {@code Decimal14f} constant 0.01.*/
	public static final Decimal14f HUNDREDTH = new Decimal14f(ONE_UNSCALED / 100);
	/** The {@code Decimal14f} constant 0.001.*/
	public static final Decimal14f THOUSANDTH = new Decimal14f(ONE_UNSCALED / 1000);
	/** The {@code Decimal14f} constant 10<sup>-6</sup>.*/
	public static final Decimal14f MILLIONTH = new Decimal14f(ONE_UNSCALED / 1000000);
	/** The {@code Decimal14f} constant 10<sup>-9</sup>.*/
	public static final Decimal14f BILLIONTH = new Decimal14f(ONE_UNSCALED / 1000000000);
	/** The {@code Decimal14f} constant 10<sup>-12</sup>.*/
	public static final Decimal14f TRILLIONTH = new Decimal14f(ONE_UNSCALED / 1000000000000L);

    /**
     * A constant holding the maximum value a {@code Decimal14f} can have,
     * 92233.72036854775807.
     */
	public static final Decimal14f MAX_VALUE = new Decimal14f(Long.MAX_VALUE);
    /**
     * A constant holding the maximum integer value a {@code Decimal14f}
     * can have, 92233.00000000000000.
     */
	public static final Decimal14f MAX_INTEGER_VALUE = new Decimal14f((Long.MAX_VALUE / ONE_UNSCALED) * ONE_UNSCALED);
    /**
     * A constant holding the minimum value a {@code Decimal14f} can have,
     * -92233.72036854775808.
     */
	public static final Decimal14f MIN_VALUE = new Decimal14f(Long.MIN_VALUE);
    /**
     * A constant holding the minimum integer value a {@code Decimal14f}
     * can have, -92233.00000000000000.
     */
	public static final Decimal14f MIN_INTEGER_VALUE = new Decimal14f((Long.MIN_VALUE / ONE_UNSCALED) * ONE_UNSCALED);

	/**
	 * Private constructor with unscaled value.
	 *
	 * @param unscaled the unscaled value
	 */
	private Decimal14f(long unscaled) {
		super(unscaled);
	}

	/**
	 * Translates the string representation of a {@code Decimal} into a
	 * {@code Decimal14f}. The string representation consists of an
	 * optional sign, {@code '+'} or {@code '-'} , followed by a sequence of
	 * zero or more decimal digits ("the integer"), optionally followed by a
	 * fraction.
	 * <p>
	 * The fraction consists of a decimal point followed by zero or more decimal
	 * digits. The string must contain at least one digit in either the integer
	 * or the fraction. If the fraction contains more than 14 digits, the 
	 * value is rounded using {@link RoundingMode#HALF_UP HALF_UP} rounding. An 
	 * exception is thrown if the value is too large to be represented as a 
	 * {@code Decimal14f}.
	 *
	 * @param value
	 *            String value to convert into a {@code Decimal14f}
	 * @throws NumberFormatException
	 *             if {@code value} does not represent a valid {@code Decimal}
	 *             or if the value is too large to be represented as a 
	 *             {@code Decimal14f}
	 */
	public Decimal14f(String value) {
		super(DEFAULT_CHECKED_ARITHMETIC.parse(value));
	}
	
	@Override
	public final Scale14f getScaleMetrics() {
		return METRICS;
	}

	@Override
	public final int getScale() {
		return SCALE;
	}

	@Override
	public final Factory14f getFactory() {
		return FACTORY;
	}

	@Override
	protected final Decimal14f self() {
		return this;
	}

	@Override
	protected final DecimalArithmetic getDefaultArithmetic() {
		return DEFAULT_ARITHMETIC;
	}
	
	@Override
	protected final DecimalArithmetic getDefaultCheckedArithmetic() {
		return DEFAULT_CHECKED_ARITHMETIC;
	}
	
	@Override
	protected final DecimalArithmetic getRoundingDownArithmetic() {
		return METRICS.getRoundingDownArithmetic();
	}
	
	@Override
	protected final DecimalArithmetic getRoundingFloorArithmetic() {
		return METRICS.getRoundingFloorArithmetic();
	}
	
	@Override
	protected final DecimalArithmetic getRoundingHalfEvenArithmetic() {
		return METRICS.getRoundingHalfEvenArithmetic();
	}
	
	@Override
	protected final DecimalArithmetic getRoundingUnnecessaryArithmetic() {
		return METRICS.getRoundingUnnecessaryArithmetic();
	}

 	/**
	 * Returns a {@code Decimal14f} whose value is numerically equal to
	 * that of the specified {@code long} value. An exception is thrown if the
	 * specified value is too large to be represented as a {@code Decimal14f}.
	 *
	 * @param value
	 *            long value to convert into a {@code Decimal14f}
	 * @return a {@code Decimal14f} value numerically equal to the specified 
	 *            {@code long} value
	 * @throws IllegalArgumentException
	 *            if {@code value} is too large to be represented as a 
	 *            {@code Decimal14f}
	 */
	public static Decimal14f valueOf(long value) {
        if (value == 0)
            return ZERO;
        if (value > 0 & value <= MAX_CONSTANT)
            return POS_CONST[(int) value];
        else if (value < 0 & value >= -MAX_CONSTANT)
            return NEG_CONST[(int) -value];
		return valueOfUnscaled(DEFAULT_CHECKED_ARITHMETIC.fromLong(value));
	}

	/**
	 * Returns a {@code Decimal14f} whose value is calculated by
	 * rounding the specified {@code float} argument to scale 14
	 * using {@link RoundingMode#HALF_UP HALF_UP} rounding. An exception is thrown
	 * if the specified value is too large to be represented as a {@code Decimal14f}. 
	 *
	 * @param value
	 *            float value to convert into a {@code Decimal14f}
	 * @return a {@code Decimal14f} calculated as: <tt>round<sub>HALF_UP</sub>(value)</tt>
	 * @throws IllegalArgumentException
	 *             if {@code value} is NaN or infinite or if the magnitude is
	 *             too large for the float to be represented as a {@code Decimal14f}
	 */
	public static Decimal14f valueOf(float value) {
		return valueOfUnscaled(DEFAULT_CHECKED_ARITHMETIC.fromFloat(value));
	}

	/**
	 * Returns a {@code Decimal14f} whose value is calculated by
	 * rounding the specified {@code float} argument to scale 14
	 * using the specified {@code roundingMode}. An exception is thrown
	 * if the specified value is too large to be represented as a {@code Decimal14f}. 
	 *
	 * @param value
	 *            float value to convert into a {@code Decimal14f}
	 * @param roundingMode
	 *            the rounding mode to apply during the conversion if necessary
	 * @return a {@code Decimal14f} calculated as: <tt>round(value)</tt>
	 * @throws IllegalArgumentException
	 *             if {@code value} is NaN or infinite or if the magnitude is
	 *             too large for the float to be represented as a {@code Decimal14f}
	 * @throws ArithmeticException
	 *             if {@code roundingMode==UNNECESSARY} and rounding is
	 *             necessary
	 */
	public static Decimal14f valueOf(float value, RoundingMode roundingMode) {
		return valueOfUnscaled(METRICS.getCheckedArithmetic(roundingMode).fromFloat(value));
	}

	/**
	 * Returns a {@code Decimal14f} whose value is calculated by
	 * rounding the specified {@code double} argument to scale 14
	 * using {@link RoundingMode#HALF_UP HALF_UP} rounding. An exception is thrown
	 * if the specified value is too large to be represented as a {@code Decimal14f}. 
	 *
	 * @param value
	 *            double value to convert into a {@code Decimal14f}
	 * @return a {@code Decimal14f} calculated as: <tt>round<sub>HALF_UP</sub>(value)</tt>
	 * @throws IllegalArgumentException
	 *             if {@code value} is NaN or infinite or if the magnitude is
	 *             too large for the double to be represented as a {@code Decimal14f}
	 */
	public static Decimal14f valueOf(double value) {
		return valueOfUnscaled(DEFAULT_CHECKED_ARITHMETIC.fromDouble(value));
	}

	/**
	 * Returns a {@code Decimal14f} whose value is calculated by
	 * rounding the specified {@code double} argument to scale 14
	 * using the specified {@code roundingMode}. An exception is thrown
	 * if the specified value is too large to be represented as a {@code Decimal14f}. 
	 *
	 * @param value
	 *            double value to convert into a {@code Decimal14f}
	 * @param roundingMode
	 *            the rounding mode to apply during the conversion if necessary
	 * @return a {@code Decimal14f} calculated as: <tt>round(value)</tt>
	 * @throws IllegalArgumentException
	 *             if {@code value} is NaN or infinite or if the magnitude is
	 *             too large for the double to be represented as a {@code Decimal14f}
	 * @throws ArithmeticException
	 *             if {@code roundingMode==UNNECESSARY} and rounding is
	 *             necessary
	 */
	public static Decimal14f valueOf(double value, RoundingMode roundingMode) {
		return valueOfUnscaled(METRICS.getCheckedArithmetic(roundingMode).fromDouble(value));
	}

	/**
	 * Returns a {@code Decimal14f} whose value is numerically equal to that of
	 * the specified {@link BigInteger} value. An exception is thrown if the
	 * specified value is too large to be represented as a {@code Decimal14f}.
	 *
	 * @param value
	 *            {@code BigInteger} value to convert into a {@code Decimal14f}
	 * @return a {@code Decimal14f} value numerically equal to the specified big 
	 *         integer value
	 * @throws IllegalArgumentException
	 *             if {@code value} is too large to be represented as a {@code Decimal14f}
	 */
	public static Decimal14f valueOf(BigInteger value) {
		return valueOfUnscaled(DEFAULT_CHECKED_ARITHMETIC.fromBigInteger(value));
	}

	/**
	 * Returns a {@code Decimal14f} whose value is calculated by rounding
	 * the specified {@link BigDecimal} argument to scale 14 using
	 * {@link RoundingMode#HALF_UP HALF_UP} rounding. An exception is thrown if the 
	 * specified value is too large to be represented as a {@code Decimal14f}.
	 *
	 * @param value
	 *            {@code BigDecimal} value to convert into a {@code Decimal14f}
	 * @return a {@code Decimal14f} calculated as: <tt>round<sub>HALF_UP</sub>(value)</tt>
	 * @throws IllegalArgumentException
	 *             if {@code value} is too large to be represented as a {@code Decimal14f}
	 */
	public static Decimal14f valueOf(BigDecimal value) {
		return valueOfUnscaled(DEFAULT_CHECKED_ARITHMETIC.fromBigDecimal(value));
	}

	/**
	 * Returns a {@code Decimal14f} whose value is calculated by rounding
	 * the specified {@link BigDecimal} argument to scale 14 using 
	 * the specified {@code roundingMode}. An exception is thrown if the 
	 * specified value is too large to be represented as a {@code Decimal14f}.
	 *
	 * @param value
	 *            {@code BigDecimal} value to convert into a {@code Decimal14f}
	 * @param roundingMode
	 *            the rounding mode to apply during the conversion if necessary
	 * @return a {@code Decimal14f} calculated as: <tt>round(value)</tt>
	 * @throws IllegalArgumentException
	 *             if {@code value} is too large to be represented as a {@code Decimal14f}
	 * @throws ArithmeticException
	 *             if {@code roundingMode==UNNECESSARY} and rounding is
	 *             necessary
	 */
	public static Decimal14f valueOf(BigDecimal value, RoundingMode roundingMode) {
		return valueOfUnscaled(METRICS.getCheckedArithmetic(roundingMode).fromBigDecimal(value));
	}

	/**
	 * Returns a {@code Decimal14f} whose value is calculated by rounding
	 * the specified {@link Decimal} argument to scale 14 using
	 * {@link RoundingMode#HALF_UP HALF_UP} rounding. An exception is thrown if the
	 * specified value is too large to be represented as a {@code Decimal14f}. 
	 *
	 * @param value
	 *            Decimal value to convert into a {@code Decimal14f} 
	 * @return a {@code Decimal14f} calculated as: <tt>round<sub>HALF_UP</sub>(value)</tt>
	 * @throws IllegalArgumentException
	 *             if {@code value} is too large to be represented as a {@code Decimal14f}
	 */
	public static Decimal14f valueOf(Decimal<?> value) {
		if (value instanceof Decimal14f) {
			return (Decimal14f)value;
		}
		return valueOfUnscaled(value.unscaledValue(), value.getScale());
	}

	/**
	 * Returns a {@code Decimal14f} whose value is calculated by rounding
	 * the specified {@link Decimal} argument to scale 14 using
	 * the specified {@code roundingMode}. An exception is thrown if the
	 * specified value is too large to be represented as a {@code Decimal14f}. 
	 *
	 * @param value
	 *            Decimal value to convert into a {@code Decimal14f} 
	 * @param roundingMode
	 *            the rounding mode to apply during the conversion if necessary
	 * @return a {@code Decimal14f} calculated as: <tt>round(value)</tt>
	 * @throws IllegalArgumentException
	 *             if {@code value} is too large to be represented as a {@code Decimal14f}
	 * @throws ArithmeticException
	 *             if {@code roundingMode==UNNECESSARY} and rounding is
	 *             necessary
	 */
	public static Decimal14f valueOf(Decimal<?> value, RoundingMode roundingMode) {
		if (value instanceof Decimal14f) {
			return (Decimal14f)value;
		}
		return valueOfUnscaled(value.unscaledValue(), value.getScale(), roundingMode);
	}

	/**
	 * Translates the string representation of a {@code Decimal} into a
	 * {@code Decimal14f}. The string representation consists of an
	 * optional sign, {@code '+'} or {@code '-'} , followed by a sequence of
	 * zero or more decimal digits ("the integer"), optionally followed by a
	 * fraction.
	 * <p>
	 * The fraction consists of a decimal point followed by zero or more decimal
	 * digits. The string must contain at least one digit in either the integer
	 * or the fraction. If the fraction contains more than 14 digits, the 
	 * value is rounded using {@link RoundingMode#HALF_UP HALF_UP} rounding. An 
	 * exception is thrown if the value is too large to be represented as a 
	 * {@code Decimal14f}.
	 *
	 * @param value
	 *            String value to convert into a {@code Decimal14f}
	 * @return a {@code Decimal14f} calculated as: <tt>round<sub>HALF_UP</sub>(value)</tt>

		return valueOfUnscaled(DEFAULT_CHECKED_ARITHMETIC.parse(value));
	}

	 * {@code Decimal14f}. The string representation consists of an
	 * optional sign, {@code '+'} or {@code '-'} , followed by a sequence of
	 * zero or more decimal digits ("the integer"), optionally followed by a
	 * fraction.

	 * The fraction consists of a decimal point followed by zero or more decimal
	 * digits. The string must contain at least one digit in either the integer
	 * or the fraction. If the fraction contains more than 14 digits, the 
	 * value is rounded using the specified {@code roundingMode}. An exception 
	 * is thrown if the value is too large to be represented as a {@code Decimal14f}.
	 *
	 * @param value
	 *            String value to convert into a {@code Decimal14f}
	 * @param roundingMode

	 *            14 digits

	 *             or if the value is too large to be represented as a

	 *             if {@code roundingMode==UNNECESSARY} and rounding is
	 *             necessary

		return valueOfUnscaled(METRICS.getCheckedArithmetic(roundingMode).parse(value));

	 * @return a {@code Decimal14f} calculated as:

	public static Decimal14f valueOfUnscaled(long unscaledValue) {
		if (unscaledValue == 0) {
			return ZERO;
		}
		if (unscaledValue == 1) {
			return ULP;
		}
		if (unscaledValue == ONE_UNSCALED) {
			return ONE;
		}
		if (unscaledValue == -ONE_UNSCALED) {
			return MINUS_ONE;
		}
		return new Decimal14f(unscaledValue);

	}

	@Override
	protected Decimal14f createOrAssign(long unscaled) {

	}
	
	@Override

# decimal4j 1.0.3 - public API surface

decimal4j (`org.decimal4j`) is a fixed-point arithmetic library. A value is a
`long` unscaled number plus a *scale* (0–18 decimal places) that is fixed at
compile time, so arithmetic is plain `long` arithmetic with no allocation and no
`BigDecimal`. The library ships a specialisation per scale: `Decimal0f` …
`Decimal18f` (immutable), `MutableDecimal0f` … `MutableDecimal18f`, plus
`Scale0f` … `Scale18f` and `Factory0f` … `Factory18f`.

Everything is CPU-bound and allocation-light. Benchmarks should build the input
values in `@Setup` and measure one operation kind per method; the interesting
comparisons are against `BigDecimal` and against `double`.

## Values

`org.decimal4j.immutable.Decimal5f` (the same shape for every scale)
- constants `ZERO`, `ULP`, `ONE`, `TWO`, … `TEN`, `HUNDRED`, `THOUSAND`,
  `MINUS_ONE`, `HALF`, `TENTH`, `MAX_VALUE`, `MIN_VALUE`
- `static Decimal5f valueOf(long|float|double|BigInteger|BigDecimal|String|Decimal<?>)`,
  each with a `RoundingMode` overload
- `static Decimal5f unscaled(long unscaledValue)`,
  `static Decimal5f unscaled(long unscaledValue, int scale)`

`org.decimal4j.mutable.MutableDecimal5f`
- `MutableDecimal5f()`, and constructors taking
  `long|double|String|BigInteger|BigDecimal|Decimal<?>`
- `static MutableDecimal5f zero()`, `one()`, `two()`, … `ten()`,
  `static MutableDecimal5f unscaled(long unscaledValue)`
- in-place setters: `set(...)`, `setZero()`, `setOne()`, `setMinusOne()`,
  `setUnscaled(long)`, and every arithmetic method mutates and returns `this`.

`org.decimal4j.generic.GenericImmutableDecimal` /
`GenericMutableDecimal` — scale carried at runtime rather than in the type; built
through `GenericDecimalFactory`.

## Arithmetic — `org.decimal4j.api.Decimal`

`add`, `subtract`, `multiply`, `divide`, `remainder`, `negate`, `abs`,
`invert`, `square`, `sqrt`, `pow(int)`, `avg`, `shiftLeft`, `shiftRight`,
`round(int precision)`, each with `RoundingMode` / `TruncationPolicy` overloads
and `…Unscaled(long unscaledValue[, int scale])` and `…Long(long)` variants.

- `Decimal<?> multiplyExact(Decimal<?>)` — widens the scale instead of rounding.
- `Multipliable5f multiplyExact()` — the fluent form: `a.multiplyExact().by(b)`
  returns the exact product at the summed scale (`Multipliable5f.by(Decimal6f)`
  yields a `Decimal11f`). One `Multipliable<N>f` class per scale.
- `<S extends ScaleMetrics> ImmutableDecimal<S> scale(S scaleMetrics)` and
  `scale(int scale[, RoundingMode])` — rescale to a different scale.
- `Decimal<S> multiplyUnscaled(long unscaledMultiplicand, TruncationPolicy)`.
- conversions: `longValue`, `intValue`, `doubleValue`, `floatValue`,
  `toBigDecimal`, `toBigInteger`, `unscaledValue()`, `getScale()`,
  `getScaleMetrics()`, `getFactory()`, `toString()`.

## Scale metrics — `org.decimal4j.scale`

`Scale5f.INSTANCE` (one enum constant per scale) implements `ScaleMetrics`:
- `int getScale()`, `long getScaleFactor()`, `BigInteger getScaleFactorAsBigInteger()`
- `long multiplyByScaleFactor(long)`, `long multiplyByScaleFactorExact(long)`,
  `long mulloByScaleFactor(int)`, `long mulhiByScaleFactor(int)`
- `long divideByScaleFactor(long)`, `long divideUnsignedByScaleFactor(long)`,
  `long moduloByScaleFactor(long)`
- `DecimalArithmetic getDefaultArithmetic()`, `getDefaultCheckedArithmetic()`,
  `getRoundingHalfUpArithmetic()`, `getArithmetic(RoundingMode)`,
  `getCheckedArithmetic(RoundingMode)`, `getArithmetic(TruncationPolicy)`

`org.decimal4j.scale.Scales` — `getScaleMetrics(int scale)`,
`findByScaleFactor(long)`, `VALUES`, `MIN_SCALE`, `MAX_SCALE`.

## Arithmetic back-ends — `org.decimal4j.api.DecimalArithmetic`

Obtained from `ScaleMetrics`; the implementations live in
`org.decimal4j.arithmetic` (`UncheckedScaleNfTruncatingArithmetic`,
`UncheckedScaleNfRoundingArithmetic`, `CheckedScale0fRoundingArithmetic`,
`CheckedScaleNfRoundingArithmetic`, …). All operate on raw unscaled `long`s:
- `int getScale()`, `ScaleMetrics getScaleMetrics()`, `RoundingMode getRoundingMode()`,
  `OverflowMode getOverflowMode()`, `TruncationPolicy getTruncationPolicy()`
- `long add|subtract|multiply|divide|pow|avg|invert|square|sqrt|negate|abs(long …)`
- conversions in: `fromLong(long)`, `fromFloat(float)`, `fromDouble(double)`,
  `fromBigDecimal(BigDecimal)`, `fromBigInteger(BigInteger)`,
  `fromUnscaled(long unscaledValue, int scale)`, `parse(String)`
- conversions out: `toLong`, `toFloat`, `toDouble`, `toBigDecimal`,
  `toUnscaled(long, int scale)`, `toString(long)`
- `DecimalArithmetic deriveArithmetic(RoundingMode|OverflowMode|TruncationPolicy)`

## Factories — `org.decimal4j.factory`

`Factory5f.INSTANCE` implements `DecimalFactory<Scale5f>`:
`getScale()`, `getScaleMetrics()`, `immutableType()`, `mutableType()`,
`valueOf(long|float|double|BigInteger|BigDecimal|String|Decimal<?>)` (with
`RoundingMode` overloads), `valueOfUnscaled(long[, int scale])`,
`newArray(int length)`, `newMutable()`.

`org.decimal4j.factory.Factories` — `getDecimalFactory(int|ScaleMetrics)`,
`getGenericDecimalFactory(int|ScaleMetrics)`, `VALUES`.

`org.decimal4j.generic.GenericDecimalFactory` —
`new GenericDecimalFactory<>(ScaleMetrics)` and the same `valueOf…` API,
returning `GenericImmutableDecimal` / `GenericMutableDecimal`.

## Rounding and overflow — `org.decimal4j.truncate`

- `DecimalRounding` — enum mirroring `RoundingMode`
  (`UP`, `DOWN`, `CEILING`, `FLOOR`, `HALF_UP`, `HALF_DOWN`, `HALF_EVEN`,
  `UNNECESSARY`); `getRoundingMode()`,
  `int calculateRoundingIncrement(int sign, long truncatedValue, TruncatedPart)`,
  `static DecimalRounding valueOf(RoundingMode)`.
- `TruncatedPart` — `ZERO`, `LESS_THAN_HALF_BUT_NOT_ZERO`, `EQUAL_TO_HALF`,
  `GREATER_THAN_HALF`; `boolean isGreaterThanZero()`,
  `boolean isGreaterEqualHalf()`,
  `static TruncatedPart valueOf(int firstTruncatedDigit, boolean zeroAfter)`.
- `OverflowMode` — `UNCHECKED`, `CHECKED`; `boolean isChecked()`.
- `TruncationPolicy`, and the two enums implementing it: `UncheckedRounding`
  (`toCheckedRounding()`) and `CheckedRounding` (`toUncheckedRounding()`), each
  with a constant per rounding mode and `static … valueOf(RoundingMode)`.

## Utilities — `org.decimal4j.util`

`DoubleRounder` — `new DoubleRounder(int precision)`,
`new DoubleRounder(ScaleMetrics)`, `int getPrecision()`,
`double round(double[, RoundingMode])`, and the statics
`DoubleRounder.round(double value, int precision[, RoundingMode])`.

package org.decimal4j.immutable;

import java.math.BigDecimal;
import java.math.BigInteger;
import java.math.RoundingMode;

import org.decimal4j.api.Decimal;
import org.decimal4j.api.DecimalArithmetic;
import org.decimal4j.base.AbstractImmutableDecimal;
import org.decimal4j.exact.Multipliable7f;
import org.decimal4j.factory.Factory7f;
import org.decimal4j.mutable.MutableDecimal7f;
import org.decimal4j.scale.Scale7f;

/**
 * <tt>Decimal7f</tt> represents an immutable decimal number with a fixed
 * number of 7 digits to the right of the decimal point.
 * <p>
 * All methods for this class throw {@code NullPointerException} when passed a
 * {@code null} object reference for any input parameter.
 */
public final class Decimal7f extends AbstractImmutableDecimal<Scale7f, Decimal7f> {

	private static final long serialVersionUID = 1L;

	/** Scale value 7 for {@code Decimal7f} returned by {@link #getScale()}.*/
	public static final int SCALE = 7;

	/** Scale metrics constant for {@code Decimal7f} returned by {@link #getScaleMetrics()}.*/
	public static final Scale7f METRICS = Scale7f.INSTANCE;

	/** Factory constant for {@code Decimal7f} returned by {@link #getFactory()}.*/
	public static final Factory7f FACTORY = Factory7f.INSTANCE;
	
	/**
	 * Default arithmetic for {@code Decimal7f} performing unchecked operations with rounding mode 
	 * {@link RoundingMode#HALF_UP HALF_UP}.
	 */
	public static final DecimalArithmetic DEFAULT_ARITHMETIC = METRICS.getDefaultArithmetic();
	
	/**
	 * Default arithmetic for {@code Decimal7f} performing checked operations with rounding mode 
	 * {@link RoundingMode#HALF_UP HALF_UP}.
	 */
	public static final DecimalArithmetic DEFAULT_CHECKED_ARITHMETIC = METRICS.getDefaultCheckedArithmetic();

	/** The unscaled long value that represents one.*/
	public static final long ONE_UNSCALED = METRICS.getScaleFactor();

	/** The {@code Decimal7f} constant zero.*/
	public static final Decimal7f ZERO = new Decimal7f(0);
    /**
     * A constant holding the smallest positive value a {@code Decimal7f}
     * can have, 10<sup>-7</sup>.
     */
	public static final Decimal7f ULP = new Decimal7f(1);

    /**
     * Initialize static constant array when class is loaded.
     */
    private static final int MAX_CONSTANT = 10;
    private static final Decimal7f POS_CONST[] = new Decimal7f[MAX_CONSTANT+1];
    private static final Decimal7f NEG_CONST[] = new Decimal7f[MAX_CONSTANT+1];

    static {
        for (int i = 1; i <= MAX_CONSTANT; i++) {
            POS_CONST[i] = new Decimal7f(ONE_UNSCALED * i);
            NEG_CONST[i] = new Decimal7f(-ONE_UNSCALED * i);
        }
    }

	/** The {@code Decimal7f} constant 1.*/
	public static final Decimal7f ONE = valueOf(1);
	/** The {@code Decimal7f} constant 2.*/
	public static final Decimal7f TWO = valueOf(2);
	/** The {@code Decimal7f} constant 3.*/
	public static final Decimal7f THREE = valueOf(3);
	/** The {@code Decimal7f} constant 4.*/
	public static final Decimal7f FOUR = valueOf(4);
	/** The {@code Decimal7f} constant 5.*/
	public static final Decimal7f FIVE = valueOf(5);
	/** The {@code Decimal7f} constant 6.*/
	public static final Decimal7f SIX = valueOf(6);
	/** The {@code Decimal7f} constant 7.*/
	public static final Decimal7f SEVEN = valueOf(7);
	/** The {@code Decimal7f} constant 8.*/
	public static final Decimal7f EIGHT = valueOf(8);
	/** The {@code Decimal7f} constant 9.*/
	public static final Decimal7f NINE = valueOf(9);
	/** The {@code Decimal7f} constant 10.*/
	public static final Decimal7f TEN = valueOf(10);
	/** The {@code Decimal7f} constant 100.*/
	public static final Decimal7f HUNDRED = new Decimal7f(100 * ONE_UNSCALED);
	/** The {@code Decimal7f} constant 1000.*/
	public static final Decimal7f THOUSAND = new Decimal7f(1000 * ONE_UNSCALED);
	/** The {@code Decimal7f} constant 10<sup>6</sup>.*/
	public static final Decimal7f MILLION = new Decimal7f(1000000 * ONE_UNSCALED);
	/** The {@code Decimal7f} constant 10<sup>9</sup>.*/
	public static final Decimal7f BILLION = new Decimal7f(1000000000 * ONE_UNSCALED);

	/** The {@code Decimal7f} constant -1.*/
	public static final Decimal7f MINUS_ONE = valueOf(-1);

	/** The {@code Decimal7f} constant 0.5.*/
	public static final Decimal7f HALF = new Decimal7f(ONE_UNSCALED / 2);
	/** The {@code Decimal7f} constant 0.1.*/
	public static final Decimal7f TENTH = new Decimal7f(ONE_UNSCALED / 10);
	/** The {@code Decimal7f} constant 0.01.*/
	public static final Decimal7f HUNDREDTH = new Decimal7f(ONE_UNSCALED / 100);
	/** The {@code Decimal7f} constant 0.001.*/
	public static final Decimal7f THOUSANDTH = new Decimal7f(ONE_UNSCALED / 1000);
	/** The {@code Decimal7f} constant 10<sup>-6</sup>.*/
	public static final Decimal7f MILLIONTH = new Decimal7f(ONE_UNSCALED / 1000000);

    /**
     * A constant holding the maximum value a {@code Decimal7f} can have,
     * 922337203685.4775807.
     */
	public static final Decimal7f MAX_VALUE = new Decimal7f(Long.MAX_VALUE);
    /**
     * A constant holding the maximum integer value a {@code Decimal7f}
     * can have, 922337203685.0000000.
     */
	public static final Decimal7f MAX_INTEGER_VALUE = new Decimal7f((Long.MAX_VALUE / ONE_UNSCALED) * ONE_UNSCALED);
    /**
     * A constant holding the minimum value a {@code Decimal7f} can have,
     * -922337203685.4775808.
     */
	public static final Decimal7f MIN_VALUE = new Decimal7f(Long.MIN_VALUE);
    /**
     * A constant holding the minimum integer value a {@code Decimal7f}
     * can have, -922337203685.0000000.
     */
	public static final Decimal7f MIN_INTEGER_VALUE = new Decimal7f((Long.MIN_VALUE / ONE_UNSCALED) * ONE_UNSCALED);

	/**
	 * Private constructor with unscaled value.
	 *
	 * @param unscaled the unscaled value
	 */
	private Decimal7f(long unscaled) {
		super(unscaled);
	}

	/**
	 * Translates the string representation of a {@code Decimal} into a
	 * {@code Decimal7f}. The string representation consists of an
	 * optional sign, {@code '+'} or {@code '-'} , followed by a sequence of
	 * zero or more decimal digits ("the integer"), optionally followed by a
	 * fraction.
	 * <p>
	 * The fraction consists of a decimal point followed by zero or more decimal
	 * digits. The string must contain at least one digit in either the integer
	 * or the fraction. If the fraction contains more than 7 digits, the 
	 * value is rounded using {@link RoundingMode#HALF_UP HALF_UP} rounding. An 
	 * exception is thrown if the value is too large to be represented as a 
	 * {@code Decimal7f}.
	 *
	 * @param value
	 *            String value to convert into a {@code Decimal7f}
	 * @throws NumberFormatException
	 *             if {@code value} does not represent a valid {@code Decimal}
	 *             or if the value is too large to be represented as a 
	 *             {@code Decimal7f}
	 */
	public Decimal7f(String value) {
		super(DEFAULT_CHECKED_ARITHMETIC.parse(value));
	}
	
	@Override
	public final Scale7f getScaleMetrics() {
		return METRICS;
	}

	@Override
	public final int getScale() {
		return SCALE;
	}

	@Override
	public final Factory7f getFactory() {
		return FACTORY;
	}

	@Override
	protected final Decimal7f self() {
		return this;
	}

	@Override
	protected final DecimalArithmetic getDefaultArithmetic() {
		return DEFAULT_ARITHMETIC;
	}
	
	@Override
	protected final DecimalArithmetic getDefaultCheckedArithmetic() {
		return DEFAULT_CHECKED_ARITHMETIC;
	}
	
	@Override
	protected final DecimalArithmetic getRoundingDownArithmetic() {
		return METRICS.getRoundingDownArithmetic();
	}
	
	@Override
	protected final DecimalArithmetic getRoundingFloorArithmetic() {
		return METRICS.getRoundingFloorArithmetic();
	}
	
	@Override
	protected final DecimalArithmetic getRoundingHalfEvenArithmetic() {
		return METRICS.getRoundingHalfEvenArithmetic();
	}
	
	@Override
	protected final DecimalArithmetic getRoundingUnnecessaryArithmetic() {
		return METRICS.getRoundingUnnecessaryArithmetic();
	}

 	/**
	 * Returns a {@code Decimal7f} whose value is numerically equal to
	 * that of the specified {@code long} value. An exception is thrown if the
	 * specified value is too large to be represented as a {@code Decimal7f}.
	 *
	 * @param value
	 *            long value to convert into a {@code Decimal7f}
	 * @return a {@code Decimal7f} value numerically equal to the specified 
	 *            {@code long} value
	 * @throws IllegalArgumentException
	 *            if {@code value} is too large to be represented as a 
	 *            {@code Decimal7f}
	 */
	public static Decimal7f valueOf(long value) {
        if (value == 0)
            return ZERO;
        if (value > 0 & value <= MAX_CONSTANT)
            return POS_CONST[(int) value];
        else if (value < 0 & value >= -MAX_CONSTANT)
            return NEG_CONST[(int) -value];
		return valueOfUnscaled(DEFAULT_CHECKED_ARITHMETIC.fromLong(value));
	}

	/**
	 * Returns a {@code Decimal7f} whose value is calculated by
	 * rounding the specified {@code float} argument to scale 7
	 * using {@link RoundingMode#HALF_UP HALF_UP} rounding. An exception is thrown
	 * if the specified value is too large to be represented as a {@code Decimal7f}. 
	 *
	 * @param value
	 *            float value to convert into a {@code Decimal7f}
	 * @return a {@code Decimal7f} calculated as: <tt>round<sub>HALF_UP</sub>(value)</tt>
	 * @throws IllegalArgumentException
	 *             if {@code value} is NaN or infinite or if the magnitude is
	 *             too large for the float to be represented as a {@code Decimal7f}
	 */
	public static Decimal7f valueOf(float value) {
		return valueOfUnscaled(DEFAULT_CHECKED_ARITHMETIC.fromFloat(value));
	}

	/**
	 * Returns a {@code Decimal7f} whose value is calculated by
	 * rounding the specified {@code float} argument to scale 7
	 * using the specified {@code roundingMode}. An exception is thrown

	 * @param value

	 * @throws IllegalArgumentException
	 *             if {@code value} is NaN or infinite or if the magnitude is
	 *             too large for the float to be represented as a {@code Decimal7f}
	 * @throws ArithmeticException
	 *             if {@code roundingMode==UNNECESSARY} and rounding is
	 *             necessary
	 */
	public static Decimal7f valueOf(float value, RoundingMode roundingMode) {
		return valueOfUnscaled(METRICS.getCheckedArithmetic(roundingMode).fromFloat(value));
	}

	/**

	public static Decimal7f valueOf(double value) {

	}

	public static Decimal7f valueOf(double value, RoundingMode roundingMode) {

	/**

        str = "123.456789012";
        rm = RoundingMode.HALF_UP;
        exp2 = 2;
        scale3 = 3;
        scale5 = 5;
    }
...

# decimal4j 1.0.3 - public API surface

decimal4j (`org.decimal4j`) is a fixed-point arithmetic library. A value is a
`long` unscaled number plus a *scale* (0–18 decimal places) that is fixed at
compile time, so arithmetic is plain `long` arithmetic with no allocation and no
`BigDecimal`. The library ships a specialisation per scale: `Decimal0f` …
`Decimal18f` (immutable), `MutableDecimal0f` … `MutableDecimal18f`, plus
`Scale0f` … `Scale18f` and `Factory0f` … `Factory18f`.

Everything is CPU-bound and allocation-light. Benchmarks should build the input
values in `@Setup` and measure one operation kind per method; the interesting
comparisons are against `BigDecimal` and against `double`.

## Values

`org.decimal4j.immutable.Decimal5f` (the same shape for every scale)
- constants `ZERO`, `ULP`, `ONE`, `TWO`, … `TEN`, `HUNDRED`, `THOUSAND`,
  `MINUS_ONE`, `HALF`, `TENTH`, `MAX_VALUE`, `MIN_VALUE`
- `static Decimal5f valueOf(long|float|double|BigInteger|BigDecimal|String|Decimal<?>)`,
  each with a `RoundingMode` overload
- `static Decimal5f unscaled(long unscaledValue)`,
  `static Decimal5f unscaled(long unscaledValue, int scale)`

`org.decimal4j.mutable.MutableDecimal5f`
- `MutableDecimal5f()`, and constructors taking
  `long|double|String|BigInteger|BigDecimal|Decimal<?>`
- `static MutableDecimal5f zero()`, `one()`, `two()`, … `ten()`,
  `static MutableDecimal5f unscaled(long unscaledValue)`
- in-place setters: `set(...)`, `setZero()`, `setOne()`, `setMinusOne()`,
  `setUnscaled(long)`, and every arithmetic method mutates and returns `this`.

`org.decimal4j.generic.GenericImmutableDecimal` /
`GenericMutableDecimal` — scale carried at runtime rather than in the type; built
through `GenericDecimalFactory`.

## Arithmetic — `org.decimal4j.api.Decimal`

`add`, `subtract`, `multiply`, `divide`, `remainder`, `negate`, `abs`,
`invert`, `square`, `sqrt`, `pow(int)`, `avg`, `shiftLeft`, `shiftRight`,
`round(int precision)`, each with `RoundingMode` / `TruncationPolicy` overloads
and `…Unscaled(long unscaledValue[, int scale])` and `…Long(long)` variants.

- `Decimal<?> multiplyExact(Decimal<?>)` — widens the scale instead of rounding.
- `Multipliable5f multiplyExact()` — the fluent form: `a.multiplyExact().by(b)`
  returns the exact product at the summed scale (`Multipliable5f.by(Decimal6f)`
  yields a `Decimal11f`). One `Multipliable<N>f` class per scale.
- `<S extends ScaleMetrics> ImmutableDecimal<S> scale(S scaleMetrics)` and
  `scale(int scale[, RoundingMode])` — rescale to a different scale.
- `Decimal<S> multiplyUnscaled(long unscaledMultiplicand, TruncationPolicy)`.
- conversions: `longValue`, `intValue`, `doubleValue`, `floatValue`,
  `toBigDecimal`, `toBigInteger`, `unscaledValue()`, `getScale()`,
  `getScaleMetrics()`, `getFactory()`, `toString()`.

## Scale metrics — `org.decimal4j.scale`

`Scale5f.INSTANCE` (one enum constant per scale) implements `ScaleMetrics`:
- `int getScale()`, `long getScaleFactor()`, `BigInteger getScaleFactorAsBigInteger()`
- `long multiplyByScaleFactor(long)`, `long multiplyByScaleFactorExact(long)`,
  `long mulloByScaleFactor(int)`, `long mulhiByScaleFactor(int)`
- `long divideByScaleFactor(long)`, `long divideUnsignedByScaleFactor(long)`,
  `long moduloByScaleFactor(long)`
- `DecimalArithmetic getDefaultArithmetic()`, `getDefaultCheckedArithmetic()`,
  `getRoundingHalfUpArithmetic()`, `getArithmetic(RoundingMode)`,
  `getCheckedArithmetic(RoundingMode)`, `getArithmetic(TruncationPolicy)`

`org.decimal4j.scale.Scales` — `getScaleMetrics(int scale)`,
`findByScaleFactor(long)`, `VALUES`, `MIN_SCALE`, `MAX_SCALE`.

## Arithmetic back-ends — `org.decimal4j.api.DecimalArithmetic`

Obtained from `ScaleMetrics`; the implementations live in
`org.decimal4j.arithmetic` (`UncheckedScaleNfTruncatingArithmetic`,
`UncheckedScaleNfRoundingArithmetic`, `CheckedScale0fRoundingArithmetic`,
`CheckedScaleNfRoundingArithmetic`, …). All operate on raw unscaled `long`s:
- `int getScale()`, `ScaleMetrics getScaleMetrics()`, `RoundingMode getRoundingMode()`,
  `OverflowMode getOverflowMode()`, `TruncationPolicy getTruncationPolicy()`
- `long add|subtract|multiply|divide|pow|avg|invert|square|sqrt|negate|abs(long …)`
- conversions in: `fromLong(long)`, `fromFloat(float)`, `fromDouble(double)`,
  `fromBigDecimal(BigDecimal)`, `fromBigInteger(BigInteger)`,
  `fromUnscaled(long unscaledValue, int scale)`, `parse(String)`
- conversions out: `toLong`, `toFloat`, `toDouble`, `toBigDecimal`,
  `toUnscaled(long, int scale)`, `toString(long)`
- `DecimalArithmetic deriveArithmetic(RoundingMode|OverflowMode|TruncationPolicy)`

## Factories — `org.decimal4j.factory`

`Factory5f.INSTANCE` implements `DecimalFactory<Scale5f>`:
`getScale()`, `getScaleMetrics()`, `immutableType()`, `mutableType()`,
`valueOf(long|float|double|BigInteger|BigDecimal|String|Decimal<?>)` (with
`RoundingMode` overloads), `valueOfUnscaled(long[, int scale])`,
`newArray(int length)`, `newMutable()`.

`org.decimal4j.factory.Factories` — `getDecimalFactory(int|ScaleMetrics)`,
`getGenericDecimalFactory(int|ScaleMetrics)`, `VALUES`.

`org.decimal4j.generic.GenericDecimalFactory` —
`new GenericDecimalFactory<>(ScaleMetrics)` and the same `valueOf…` API,
returning `GenericImmutableDecimal` / `GenericMutableDecimal`.

## Rounding and overflow — `org.decimal4j.truncate`

- `DecimalRounding` — enum mirroring `RoundingMode`
  (`UP`, `DOWN`, `CEILING`, `FLOOR`, `HALF_UP`, `HALF_DOWN`, `HALF_EVEN`,
  `UNNECESSARY`); `getRoundingMode()`,
  `int calculateRoundingIncrement(int sign, long truncatedValue, TruncatedPart)`,
  `static DecimalRounding valueOf(RoundingMode)`.
- `TruncatedPart` — `ZERO`, `LESS_THAN_HALF_BUT_NOT_ZERO`, `EQUAL_TO_HALF`,
  `GREATER_THAN_HALF`; `boolean isGreaterThanZero()`,
  `boolean isGreaterEqualHalf()`,
  `static TruncatedPart valueOf(int firstTruncatedDigit, boolean zeroAfter)`.
- `OverflowMode` — `UNCHECKED`, `CHECKED`; `boolean isChecked()`.
- `TruncationPolicy`, and the two enums implementing it: `UncheckedRounding`
  (`toCheckedRounding()`) and `CheckedRounding` (`toUncheckedRounding()`), each
  with a constant per rounding mode and `static … valueOf(RoundingMode)`.

## Utilities — `org.decimal4j.util`

`DoubleRounder` — `new DoubleRounder(int precision)`,
`new DoubleRounder(ScaleMetrics)`, `int getPrecision()`,
`double round(double[, RoundingMode])`, and the statics
`DoubleRounder.round(double value, int precision[, RoundingMode])`.

/**
 * <tt>MutableDecimal10f</tt> represents a mutable decimal number with a fixed
 * number of 10 digits to the right of the decimal point.
 * <p>
 * All methods for this class throw {@code NullPointerException} when passed a

	 * fraction.

	 * The fraction consists of a decimal point followed by zero or more decimal
	 * digits. The string must contain at least one digit in either the integer
	 * or the fraction. If the fraction contains more than 10 digits, the 
	 * value is rounded using {@link RoundingMode#HALF_UP HALF_UP} rounding. An 
	 * exception is thrown if the value is too large to be represented as a 
	 * {@code MutableDecimal10f}.

	 * @param value

	 * @throws NumberFormatException

# decimal4j 1.0.3 - public API surface

decimal4j (`org.decimal4j`) is a fixed-point arithmetic library. A value is a
`long` unscaled number plus a *scale* (0–18 decimal places) that is fixed at
compile time, so arithmetic is plain `long` arithmetic with no allocation and no
`BigDecimal`. The library ships a specialisation per scale: `Decimal0f` …
`Decimal18f` (immutable), `MutableDecimal0f` … `MutableDecimal18f`, plus
`Scale0f` … `Scale18f` and `Factory0f` … `Factory18f`.

Everything is CPU-bound and allocation-light. Benchmarks should build the input
values in `@Setup` and measure one operation kind per method; the interesting
comparisons are against `BigDecimal` and against `double`.

## Values

`org.decimal4j.immutable.Decimal5f` (the same shape for every scale)
- constants `ZERO`, `ULP`, `ONE`, `TWO`, … `TEN`, `HUNDRED`, `THOUSAND`,
  `MINUS_ONE`, `HALF`, `TENTH`, `MAX_VALUE`, `MIN_VALUE`
- `static Decimal5f valueOf(long|float|double|BigInteger|BigDecimal|String|Decimal<?>)`,
  each with a `RoundingMode` overload
- `static Decimal5f unscaled(long unscaledValue)`,
  `static Decimal5f unscaled(long unscaledValue, int scale)`

`org.decimal4j.mutable.MutableDecimal5f`
- `MutableDecimal5f()`, and constructors taking
  `long|double|String|BigInteger|BigDecimal|Decimal<?>`
- `static MutableDecimal5f zero()`, `one()`, `two()`, … `ten()`,
  `static MutableDecimal5f unscaled(long unscaledValue)`
- in-place setters: `set(...)`, `setZero()`, `setOne()`, `setMinusOne()`,
  `setUnscaled(long)`, and every arithmetic method mutates and returns `this`.

`org.decimal4j.generic.GenericImmutableDecimal` /
`GenericMutableDecimal` — scale carried at runtime rather than in the type; built
through `GenericDecimalFactory`.

## Arithmetic — `org.decimal4j.api.Decimal`

`add`, `subtract`, `multiply`, `divide`, `remainder`, `negate`, `abs`,
`invert`, `square`, `sqrt`, `pow(int)`, `avg`, `shiftLeft`, `shiftRight`,
`round(int precision)`, each with `RoundingMode` / `TruncationPolicy` overloads
and `…Unscaled(long unscaledValue[, int scale])` and `…Long(long)` variants.

- `Decimal<?> multiplyExact(Decimal<?>)` — widens the scale instead of rounding.
- `Multipliable5f multiplyExact()` — the fluent form: `a.multiplyExact().by(b)`
  returns the exact product at the summed scale (`Multipliable5f.by(Decimal6f)`
  yields a `Decimal11f`). One `Multipliable<N>f` class per scale.
- `<S extends ScaleMetrics> ImmutableDecimal<S> scale(S scaleMetrics)` and
  `scale(int scale[, RoundingMode])` — rescale to a different scale.
- `Decimal<S> multiplyUnscaled(long unscaledMultiplicand, TruncationPolicy)`.
- conversions: `longValue`, `intValue`, `doubleValue`, `floatValue`,
  `toBigDecimal`, `toBigInteger`, `unscaledValue()`, `getScale()`,
  `getScaleMetrics()`, `getFactory()`, `toString()`.

## Scale metrics — `org.decimal4j.scale`

`Scale5f.INSTANCE` (one enum constant per scale) implements `ScaleMetrics`:
- `int getScale()`, `long getScaleFactor()`, `BigInteger getScaleFactorAsBigInteger()`
- `long multiplyByScaleFactor(long)`, `long multiplyByScaleFactorExact(long)`,
  `long mulloByScaleFactor(int)`, `long mulhiByScaleFactor(int)`
- `long divideByScaleFactor(long)`, `long divideUnsignedByScaleFactor(long)`,
  `long moduloByScaleFactor(long)`
- `DecimalArithmetic getDefaultArithmetic()`, `getDefaultCheckedArithmetic()`,
  `getRoundingHalfUpArithmetic()`, `getArithmetic(RoundingMode)`,
  `getCheckedArithmetic(RoundingMode)`, `getArithmetic(TruncationPolicy)`

`org.decimal4j.scale.Scales` — `getScaleMetrics(int scale)`,
`findByScaleFactor(long)`, `VALUES`, `MIN_SCALE`, `MAX_SCALE`.

## Arithmetic back-ends — `org.decimal4j.api.DecimalArithmetic`

Obtained from `ScaleMetrics`; the implementations live in
`org.decimal4j.arithmetic` (`UncheckedScaleNfTruncatingArithmetic`,
`UncheckedScaleNfRoundingArithmetic`, `CheckedScale0fRoundingArithmetic`,
`CheckedScaleNfRoundingArithmetic`, …). All operate on raw unscaled `long`s:
- `int getScale()`, `ScaleMetrics getScaleMetrics()`, `RoundingMode getRoundingMode()`,
  `OverflowMode getOverflowMode()`, `TruncationPolicy getTruncationPolicy()`
- `long add|subtract|multiply|divide|pow|avg|invert|square|sqrt|negate|abs(long …)`
- conversions in: `fromLong(long)`, `fromFloat(float)`, `fromDouble(double)`,
  `fromBigDecimal(BigDecimal)`, `fromBigInteger(BigInteger)`,
  `fromUnscaled(long unscaledValue, int scale)`, `parse(String)`
- conversions out: `toLong`, `toFloat`, `toDouble`, `toBigDecimal`,
  `toUnscaled(long, int scale)`, `toString(long)`
- `DecimalArithmetic deriveArithmetic(RoundingMode|OverflowMode|TruncationPolicy)`

## Factories — `org.decimal4j.factory`

`Factory5f.INSTANCE` implements `DecimalFactory<Scale5f>`:
`getScale()`, `getScaleMetrics()`, `immutableType()`, `mutableType()`,
`valueOf(long|float|double|BigInteger|BigDecimal|String|Decimal<?>)` (with
`RoundingMode` overloads), `valueOfUnscaled(long[, int scale])`,
`newArray(int length)`, `newMutable()`.

`org.decimal4j.factory.Factories` — `getDecimalFactory(int|ScaleMetrics)`,
`getGenericDecimalFactory(int|ScaleMetrics)`, `VALUES`.

`org.decimal4j.generic.GenericDecimalFactory` —
`new GenericDecimalFactory<>(ScaleMetrics)` and the same `valueOf…` API,
returning `GenericImmutableDecimal` / `GenericMutableDecimal`.

## Rounding and overflow — `org.decimal4j.truncate`

- `DecimalRounding` — enum mirroring `RoundingMode`
  (`UP`, `DOWN`, `CEILING`, `FLOOR`, `HALF_UP`, `HALF_DOWN`, `HALF_EVEN`,
  `UNNECESSARY`); `getRoundingMode()`,
  `int calculateRoundingIncrement(int sign, long truncatedValue, TruncatedPart)`,
  `static DecimalRounding valueOf(RoundingMode)`.
- `TruncatedPart` — `ZERO`, `LESS_THAN_HALF_BUT_NOT_ZERO`, `EQUAL_TO_HALF`,
  `GREATER_THAN_HALF`; `boolean isGreaterThanZero()`,
  `boolean isGreaterEqualHalf()`,
  `static TruncatedPart valueOf(int firstTruncatedDigit, boolean zeroAfter)`.
- `OverflowMode` — `UNCHECKED`, `CHECKED`; `boolean isChecked()`.
- `TruncationPolicy`, and the two enums implementing it: `UncheckedRounding`
  (`toCheckedRounding()`) and `CheckedRounding` (`toUncheckedRounding()`), each
  with a constant per rounding mode and `static … valueOf(RoundingMode)`.

## Utilities — `org.decimal4j.util`

`DoubleRounder` — `new DoubleRounder(int precision)`,
`new DoubleRounder(ScaleMetrics)`, `int getPrecision()`,
`double round(double[, RoundingMode])`, and the statics
`DoubleRounder.round(double value, int precision[, RoundingMode])`.

package org.decimal4j.mutable;

/**
 * <tt>MutableDecimal13f</tt> represents a mutable decimal number with a fixed
 * number of 13 digits to the right of the decimal point.
 * <p>
 * All methods for this class throw {@code NullPointerException} when passed a
 * {@code null} object reference for any input parameter.
 */
public final class MutableDecimal13f extends AbstractMutableDecimal<Scale13f, MutableDecimal13f> implements Cloneable {

	private static final long serialVersionUID = 1L;

	 * Constructs a new {@code MutableDecimal13f} with value zero.
	 * @see #zero()

		super(0);

	 *						from {@link #MutableDecimal13f(long)}

	private MutableDecimal13f(long unscaledValue, Scale13f scale) {
		super(unscaledValue);
	}

	 * Translates the string representation of a {@code Decimal} into a
	 * {@code MutableDecimal13f}. The string representation consists 
	 * of an optional sign, {@code '+'} or {@code '-'} , followed by a sequence 
	 * of zero or more decimal digits ("the integer"), optionally followed by a
	 * fraction.
	 * <p>
	 * The fraction consists of a decimal point followed by zero or more decimal
	 * digits. The string must contain at least one digit in either the integer
	 * or the fraction. If the fraction contains more than 13 digits, the 
	 * value is rounded using {@link RoundingMode#HALF_UP HALF_UP} rounding. An 
	 * exception is thrown if the value is too large to be represented as a 
	 * {@code MutableDecimal13f}.
	 *
	 * @param value
	 *            String value to convert into a {@code MutableDecimal13f}
	 * @throws NumberFormatException
	 *             if {@code value} does not represent a valid {@code Decimal}
	 *             or if the value is too large to be represented as a 
	 *             {@code MutableDecimal13f}
	 * @see #set(String, RoundingMode)
	 */
	public MutableDecimal13f(String value) {
		this();
		set(value);
	}

 	/**
	 * Constructs a {@code MutableDecimal13f} whose value is numerically equal 
	 * to that of the specified {@code long} value. An exception is thrown if the

	 *            long value to convert into a {@code MutableDecimal13f}
	 * @throws IllegalArgumentException
	 *            if {@code value} is too large to be represented as a

	}

package bench.generated;

import org.openjdk.jmh.annotations.*;
import org.openjdk.jmh.infra.Blackhole;
import java.util.concurrent.TimeUnit;
import java.math.BigDecimal;
import java.math.BigInteger;
import java.math.RoundingMode;

import org.decimal4j.mutable.MutableDecimal13f;
import org.decimal4j.immutable.Decimal13f;
import org.decimal4j.immutable.Decimal0f;
import org.decimal4j.api.Decimal;

@State(Scope.Benchmark)
@BenchmarkMode(Mode.AverageTime)
@OutputTimeUnit(TimeUnit.NANOSECONDS)
@Fork(1)
@Warmup(iterations = 1, time = 1)
@Measurement(iterations = 3, time = 1)
public class MutableDecimal13fBenchmark {

    @State(Scope.Benchmark)
    public static class BenchmarkState {
        MutableDecimal13f[] pool;
        int index;
        MutableDecimal13f readOnly;
        MutableDecimal13f b;
        BigDecimal bigDecimalValue;
        String stringValue;
        double doubleValue;
        long longValue;
        BigInteger bigIntegerValue;
        Decimal13f decimal13fValue;
        Decimal<?> decimalValue;
        Decimal0f decimal0fValue;

        @Setup(Level.Trial)
        public void setup() {
            pool = new MutableDecimal13f[1024];
            for (int i = 0; i < pool.length; i++) {
                pool[i] = MutableDecimal13f.unscaled(1234567890123456789L + i);
            }
            index = 0;
            readOnly = MutableDecimal13f.unscaled(1234567890123456789L);
            b = new MutableDecimal13f("2.5");
            bigDecimalValue = new BigDecimal("1234567890123456789.1234567890123");
            stringValue = "1234567890123456789.1234567890123";
            doubleValue = 1234567890123456789.1234567890123;
            longValue = 1234567890123456789L;
            bigIntegerValue = new BigInteger("1234567890123456789");
            decimal13fValue = Decimal13f.valueOf("1234567890123456789.1234567890123");
            decimalValue = decimal13fValue;
            decimal0fValue = Decimal0f.valueOf(1234567890L);
        }

        public MutableDecimal13f next() {
            return pool[index++ & (pool.length - 1)];
        }
    }

    @Benchmark
    public MutableDecimal13f newMutableDecimal13f(BenchmarkState state) {
        return new MutableDecimal13f();
    }

        return new MutableDecimal13f(state.longValue);
    }

    public MutableDecimal13f newMutableDecimal13fDouble(BenchmarkState state) {
        return new MutableDecimal13f(state.doubleValue);

# decimal4j 1.0.3 - public API surface

decimal4j (`org.decimal4j`) is a fixed-point arithmetic library. A value is a
`long` unscaled number plus a *scale* (0–18 decimal places) that is fixed at
compile time, so arithmetic is plain `long` arithmetic with no allocation and no
`BigDecimal`. The library ships a specialisation per scale: `Decimal0f` …
`Decimal18f` (immutable), `MutableDecimal0f` … `MutableDecimal18f`, plus
`Scale0f` … `Scale18f` and `Factory0f` … `Factory18f`.

Everything is CPU-bound and allocation-light. Benchmarks should build the input
values in `@Setup` and measure one operation kind per method; the interesting
comparisons are against `BigDecimal` and against `double`.

## Values

`org.decimal4j.immutable.Decimal5f` (the same shape for every scale)
- constants `ZERO`, `ULP`, `ONE`, `TWO`, … `TEN`, `HUNDRED`, `THOUSAND`,
  `MINUS_ONE`, `HALF`, `TENTH`, `MAX_VALUE`, `MIN_VALUE`
- `static Decimal5f valueOf(long|float|double|BigInteger|BigDecimal|String|Decimal<?>)`,
  each with a `RoundingMode` overload
- `static Decimal5f unscaled(long unscaledValue)`,
  `static Decimal5f unscaled(long unscaledValue, int scale)`

`org.decimal4j.mutable.MutableDecimal5f`
- `MutableDecimal5f()`, and constructors taking
  `long|double|String|BigInteger|BigDecimal|Decimal<?>`
- `static MutableDecimal5f zero()`, `one()`, `two()`, … `ten()`,
  `static MutableDecimal5f unscaled(long unscaledValue)`
- in-place setters: `set(...)`, `setZero()`, `setOne()`, `setMinusOne()`,
  `setUnscaled(long)`, and every arithmetic method mutates and returns `this`.

`org.decimal4j.generic.GenericImmutableDecimal` /
`GenericMutableDecimal` — scale carried at runtime rather than in the type; built
through `GenericDecimalFactory`.

## Arithmetic — `org.decimal4j.api.Decimal`

`add`, `subtract`, `multiply`, `divide`, `remainder`, `negate`, `abs`,
`invert`, `square`, `sqrt`, `pow(int)`, `avg`, `shiftLeft`, `shiftRight`,
`round(int precision)`, each with `RoundingMode` / `TruncationPolicy` overloads
and `…Unscaled(long unscaledValue[, int scale])` and `…Long(long)` variants.

- `Decimal<?> multiplyExact(Decimal<?>)` — widens the scale instead of rounding.
- `Multipliable5f multiplyExact()` — the fluent form: `a.multiplyExact().by(b)`
  returns the exact product at the summed scale (`Multipliable5f.by(Decimal6f)`
  yields a `Decimal11f`). One `Multipliable<N>f` class per scale.
- `<S extends ScaleMetrics> ImmutableDecimal<S> scale(S scaleMetrics)` and
  `scale(int scale[, RoundingMode])` — rescale to a different scale.
- `Decimal<S> multiplyUnscaled(long unscaledMultiplicand, TruncationPolicy)`.
- conversions: `longValue`, `intValue`, `doubleValue`, `floatValue`,
  `toBigDecimal`, `toBigInteger`, `unscaledValue()`, `getScale()`,
  `getScaleMetrics()`, `getFactory()`, `toString()`.

## Scale metrics — `org.decimal4j.scale`

`Scale5f.INSTANCE` (one enum constant per scale) implements `ScaleMetrics`:
- `int getScale()`, `long getScaleFactor()`, `BigInteger getScaleFactorAsBigInteger()`
- `long multiplyByScaleFactor(long)`, `long multiplyByScaleFactorExact(long)`,
  `long mulloByScaleFactor(int)`, `long mulhiByScaleFactor(int)`
- `long divideByScaleFactor(long)`, `long divideUnsignedByScaleFactor(long)`,
  `long moduloByScaleFactor(long)`
- `DecimalArithmetic getDefaultArithmetic()`, `getDefaultCheckedArithmetic()`,
  `getRoundingHalfUpArithmetic()`, `getArithmetic(RoundingMode)`,
  `getCheckedArithmetic(RoundingMode)`, `getArithmetic(TruncationPolicy)`

`org.decimal4j.scale.Scales` — `getScaleMetrics(int scale)`,
`findByScaleFactor(long)`, `VALUES`, `MIN_SCALE`, `MAX_SCALE`.

## Arithmetic back-ends — `org.decimal4j.api.DecimalArithmetic`

Obtained from `ScaleMetrics`; the implementations live in
`org.decimal4j.arithmetic` (`UncheckedScaleNfTruncatingArithmetic`,
`UncheckedScaleNfRoundingArithmetic`, `CheckedScale0fRoundingArithmetic`,
`CheckedScaleNfRoundingArithmetic`, …). All operate on raw unscaled `long`s:
- `int getScale()`, `ScaleMetrics getScaleMetrics()`, `RoundingMode getRoundingMode()`,
  `OverflowMode getOverflowMode()`, `TruncationPolicy getTruncationPolicy()`
- `long add|subtract|multiply|divide|pow|avg|invert|square|sqrt|negate|abs(long …)`
- conversions in: `fromLong(long)`, `fromFloat(float)`, `fromDouble(double)`,
  `fromBigDecimal(BigDecimal)`, `fromBigInteger(BigInteger)`,
  `fromUnscaled(long unscaledValue, int scale)`, `parse(String)`
- conversions out: `toLong`, `toFloat`, `toDouble`, `toBigDecimal`,
  `toUnscaled(long, int scale)`, `toString(long)`
- `DecimalArithmetic deriveArithmetic(RoundingMode|OverflowMode|TruncationPolicy)`

## Factories — `org.decimal4j.factory`

`Factory5f.INSTANCE` implements `DecimalFactory<Scale5f>`:
`getScale()`, `getScaleMetrics()`, `immutableType()`, `mutableType()`,
`valueOf(long|float|double|BigInteger|BigDecimal|String|Decimal<?>)` (with
`RoundingMode` overloads), `valueOfUnscaled(long[, int scale])`,
`newArray(int length)`, `newMutable()`.

`org.decimal4j.factory.Factories` — `getDecimalFactory(int|ScaleMetrics)`,
`getGenericDecimalFactory(int|ScaleMetrics)`, `VALUES`.

`org.decimal4j.generic.GenericDecimalFactory` —
`new GenericDecimalFactory<>(ScaleMetrics)` and the same `valueOf…` API,
returning `GenericImmutableDecimal` / `GenericMutableDecimal`.

## Rounding and overflow — `org.decimal4j.truncate`

- `DecimalRounding` — enum mirroring `RoundingMode`
  (`UP`, `DOWN`, `CEILING`, `FLOOR`, `HALF_UP`, `HALF_DOWN`, `HALF_EVEN`,
  `UNNECESSARY`); `getRoundingMode()`,
  `int calculateRoundingIncrement(int sign, long truncatedValue, TruncatedPart)`,
  `static DecimalRounding valueOf(RoundingMode)`.
- `TruncatedPart` — `ZERO`, `LESS_THAN_HALF_BUT_NOT_ZERO`, `EQUAL_TO_HALF`,
  `GREATER_THAN_HALF`; `boolean isGreaterThanZero()`,
  `boolean isGreaterEqualHalf()`,
  `static TruncatedPart valueOf(int firstTruncatedDigit, boolean zeroAfter)`.
- `OverflowMode` — `UNCHECKED`, `CHECKED`; `boolean isChecked()`.
- `TruncationPolicy`, and the two enums implementing it: `UncheckedRounding`
  (`toCheckedRounding()`) and `CheckedRounding` (`toUncheckedRounding()`), each
  with a constant per rounding mode and `static … valueOf(RoundingMode)`.

## Utilities — `org.decimal4j.util`

`DoubleRounder` — `new DoubleRounder(int precision)`,
`new DoubleRounder(ScaleMetrics)`, `int getPrecision()`,
`double round(double[, RoundingMode])`, and the statics
`DoubleRounder.round(double value, int precision[, RoundingMode])`.

        MutableDecimal18f[] operands;

# decimal4j 1.0.3 - public API surface

decimal4j (`org.decimal4j`) is a fixed-point arithmetic library. A value is a
`long` unscaled number plus a *scale* (0–18 decimal places) that is fixed at
compile time, so arithmetic is plain `long` arithmetic with no allocation and no
`BigDecimal`. The library ships a specialisation per scale: `Decimal0f` …
`Decimal18f` (immutable), `MutableDecimal0f` … `MutableDecimal18f`, plus
`Scale0f` … `Scale18f` and `Factory0f` … `Factory18f`.

Everything is CPU-bound and allocation-light. Benchmarks should build the input
values in `@Setup` and measure one operation kind per method; the interesting
comparisons are against `BigDecimal` and against `double`.

## Values

`org.decimal4j.immutable.Decimal5f` (the same shape for every scale)
- constants `ZERO`, `ULP`, `ONE`, `TWO`, … `TEN`, `HUNDRED`, `THOUSAND`,
  `MINUS_ONE`, `HALF`, `TENTH`, `MAX_VALUE`, `MIN_VALUE`
- `static Decimal5f valueOf(long|float|double|BigInteger|BigDecimal|String|Decimal<?>)`,
  each with a `RoundingMode` overload
- `static Decimal5f unscaled(long unscaledValue)`,
  `static Decimal5f unscaled(long unscaledValue, int scale)`

`org.decimal4j.mutable.MutableDecimal5f`
- `MutableDecimal5f()`, and constructors taking
  `long|double|String|BigInteger|BigDecimal|Decimal<?>`
- `static MutableDecimal5f zero()`, `one()`, `two()`, … `ten()`,
  `static MutableDecimal5f unscaled(long unscaledValue)`
- in-place setters: `set(...)`, `setZero()`, `setOne()`, `setMinusOne()`,
  `setUnscaled(long)`, and every arithmetic method mutates and returns `this`.

`org.decimal4j.generic.GenericImmutableDecimal` /
`GenericMutableDecimal` — scale carried at runtime rather than in the type; built
through `GenericDecimalFactory`.

## Arithmetic — `org.decimal4j.api.Decimal`

`add`, `subtract`, `multiply`, `divide`, `remainder`, `negate`, `abs`,
`invert`, `square`, `sqrt`, `pow(int)`, `avg`, `shiftLeft`, `shiftRight`,
`round(int precision)`, each with `RoundingMode` / `TruncationPolicy` overloads
and `…Unscaled(long unscaledValue[, int scale])` and `…Long(long)` variants.

- `Decimal<?> multiplyExact(Decimal<?>)` — widens the scale instead of rounding.
- `Multipliable5f multiplyExact()` — the fluent form: `a.multiplyExact().by(b)`
  returns the exact product at the summed scale (`Multipliable5f.by(Decimal6f)`
  yields a `Decimal11f`). One `Multipliable<N>f` class per scale.
- `<S extends ScaleMetrics> ImmutableDecimal<S> scale(S scaleMetrics)` and
  `scale(int scale[, RoundingMode])` — rescale to a different scale.
- `Decimal<S> multiplyUnscaled(long unscaledMultiplicand, TruncationPolicy)`.
- conversions: `longValue`, `intValue`, `doubleValue`, `floatValue`,
  `toBigDecimal`, `toBigInteger`, `unscaledValue()`, `getScale()`,
  `getScaleMetrics()`, `getFactory()`, `toString()`.

## Scale metrics — `org.decimal4j.scale`

`Scale5f.INSTANCE` (one enum constant per scale) implements `ScaleMetrics`:
- `int getScale()`, `long getScaleFactor()`, `BigInteger getScaleFactorAsBigInteger()`
- `long multiplyByScaleFactor(long)`, `long multiplyByScaleFactorExact(long)`,
  `long mulloByScaleFactor(int)`, `long mulhiByScaleFactor(int)`
- `long divideByScaleFactor(long)`, `long divideUnsignedByScaleFactor(long)`,
  `long moduloByScaleFactor(long)`
- `DecimalArithmetic getDefaultArithmetic()`, `getDefaultCheckedArithmetic()`,
  `getRoundingHalfUpArithmetic()`, `getArithmetic(RoundingMode)`,
  `getCheckedArithmetic(RoundingMode)`, `getArithmetic(TruncationPolicy)`

`org.decimal4j.scale.Scales` — `getScaleMetrics(int scale)`,
`findByScaleFactor(long)`, `VALUES`, `MIN_SCALE`, `MAX_SCALE`.

## Arithmetic back-ends — `org.decimal4j.api.DecimalArithmetic`

Obtained from `ScaleMetrics`; the implementations live in
`org.decimal4j.arithmetic` (`UncheckedScaleNfTruncatingArithmetic`,
`UncheckedScaleNfRoundingArithmetic`, `CheckedScale0fRoundingArithmetic`,
`CheckedScaleNfRoundingArithmetic`, …). All operate on raw unscaled `long`s:
- `int getScale()`, `ScaleMetrics getScaleMetrics()`, `RoundingMode getRoundingMode()`,
  `OverflowMode getOverflowMode()`, `TruncationPolicy getTruncationPolicy()`
- `long add|subtract|multiply|divide|pow|avg|invert|square|sqrt|negate|abs(long …)`
- conversions in: `fromLong(long)`, `fromFloat(float)`, `fromDouble(double)`,
  `fromBigDecimal(BigDecimal)`, `fromBigInteger(BigInteger)`,
  `fromUnscaled(long unscaledValue, int scale)`, `parse(String)`
- conversions out: `toLong`, `toFloat`, `toDouble`, `toBigDecimal`,
  `toUnscaled(long, int scale)`, `toString(long)`
- `DecimalArithmetic deriveArithmetic(RoundingMode|OverflowMode|TruncationPolicy)`

## Factories — `org.decimal4j.factory`

`Factory5f.INSTANCE` implements `DecimalFactory<Scale5f>`:
`getScale()`, `getScaleMetrics()`, `immutableType()`, `mutableType()`,
`valueOf(long|float|double|BigInteger|BigDecimal|String|Decimal<?>)` (with
`RoundingMode` overloads), `valueOfUnscaled(long[, int scale])`,
`newArray(int length)`, `newMutable()`.

`org.decimal4j.factory.Factories` — `getDecimalFactory(int|ScaleMetrics)`,
`getGenericDecimalFactory(int|ScaleMetrics)`, `VALUES`.

`org.decimal4j.generic.GenericDecimalFactory` —
`new GenericDecimalFactory<>(ScaleMetrics)` and the same `valueOf…` API,
returning `GenericImmutableDecimal` / `GenericMutableDecimal`.

## Rounding and overflow — `org.decimal4j.truncate`

- `DecimalRounding` — enum mirroring `RoundingMode`
  (`UP`, `DOWN`, `CEILING`, `FLOOR`, `HALF_UP`, `HALF_DOWN`, `HALF_EVEN`,
  `UNNECESSARY`); `getRoundingMode()`,
  `int calculateRoundingIncrement(int sign, long truncatedValue, TruncatedPart)`,
  `static DecimalRounding valueOf(RoundingMode)`.
- `TruncatedPart` — `ZERO`, `LESS_THAN_HALF_BUT_NOT_ZERO`, `EQUAL_TO_HALF`,
  `GREATER_THAN_HALF`; `boolean isGreaterThanZero()`,
  `boolean isGreaterEqualHalf()`,
  `static TruncatedPart valueOf(int firstTruncatedDigit, boolean zeroAfter)`.
- `OverflowMode` — `UNCHECKED`, `CHECKED`; `boolean isChecked()`.
- `TruncationPolicy`, and the two enums implementing it: `UncheckedRounding`
  (`toCheckedRounding()`) and `CheckedRounding` (`toUncheckedRounding()`), each
  with a constant per rounding mode and `static … valueOf(RoundingMode)`.

## Utilities — `org.decimal4j.util`

`DoubleRounder` — `new DoubleRounder(int precision)`,
`new DoubleRounder(ScaleMetrics)`, `int getPrecision()`,
`double round(double[, RoundingMode])`, and the statics
`DoubleRounder.round(double value, int precision[, RoundingMode])`.

import java.math.BigDecimal;

/**
 * <tt>MutableDecimal1f</tt> represents a mutable decimal number with a fixed
 * number of 1 digits to the right of the decimal point.
 * <p>
 * All methods for this class throw {@code NullPointerException} when passed a
 * {@code null} object reference for any input parameter.
 */
public final class MutableDecimal1f extends AbstractMutableDecimal<Scale1f, MutableDecimal1f> implements Cloneable {

	private static final long serialVersionUID = 1L;

	 * {@code MutableDecimal1f}. The string representation consists 
	 * of an optional sign, {@code '+'} or {@code '-'} , followed by a sequence 
	 * of zero or more decimal digits ("the integer"), optionally followed by a
	 * fraction.
	 * <p>
	 * The fraction consists of a decimal point followed by zero or more decimal
	 * digits. The string must contain at least one digit in either the integer
	 * or the fraction. If the fraction contains more than 1 digits, the 
	 * value is rounded using {@link RoundingMode#HALF_UP HALF_UP} rounding. An 
	 * exception is thrown if the value is too large to be represented as a 
	 * {@code MutableDecimal1f}.

	 *             {@code MutableDecimal1f}

		set(value);

@State(Scope.Thread)

@OutputTimeUnit(TimeUnit.NANOSECONDS)

@Warmup(iterations = 1, time = 1)
@Measurement(iterations = 3, time = 1)
public class MutableDecimal1fBenchmark {

    private static final int POOL_SIZE = 1024;

    private MutableDecimal1f[] receivers;
    private Decimal1f[] operands;
    private long[] longValues;
    private double[] doubleValues;
    private String[] stringValues;
    private BigDecimal[] bigDecimalValues;

    public void setup() {
        receivers = new MutableDecimal1f[POOL_SIZE];
        operands = new Decimal1f[POOL_SIZE];
        longValues = new long[POOL_SIZE];
        doubleValues = new double[POOL_SIZE];
        stringValues = new String[POOL_SIZE];
        bigDecimalValues = new BigDecimal[POOL_SIZE];

        for (int i = 0; i < POOL_SIZE; i++) {
            // Receivers: mix of positive and negative values, not too large
            double rv = (i % 2 == 0) ? (i * 1.1) : -(i * 1.1);
            receivers[i] = new MutableDecimal1f(rv);

            // Operands: non-zero, mix of signs, around 1.0 magnitude
            double ov = (i % 2 == 0) ? (1.0 + (i % 10) * 0.1) : -(1.0 + (i % 10) * 0.1);
            operands[i] = Decimal1f.valueOf(ov);

            longValues[i] = (i % 2 == 0) ? (i * 100L) : -(i * 100L);
            doubleValues[i] = (i % 2 == 0) ? (i * 0.5) : -(i * 0.5);
            stringValues[i] = (i % 2 == 0) ? (i + ".5") : ("-" + i + ".5");
            bigDecimalValues[i] = new BigDecimal(stringValues[i]);

# decimal4j 1.0.3 - public API surface

decimal4j (`org.decimal4j`) is a fixed-point arithmetic library. A value is a
`long` unscaled number plus a *scale* (0–18 decimal places) that is fixed at
compile time, so arithmetic is plain `long` arithmetic with no allocation and no
`BigDecimal`. The library ships a specialisation per scale: `Decimal0f` …
`Decimal18f` (immutable), `MutableDecimal0f` … `MutableDecimal18f`, plus
`Scale0f` … `Scale18f` and `Factory0f` … `Factory18f`.

Everything is CPU-bound and allocation-light. Benchmarks should build the input
values in `@Setup` and measure one operation kind per method; the interesting
comparisons are against `BigDecimal` and against `double`.

## Values

`org.decimal4j.immutable.Decimal5f` (the same shape for every scale)
- constants `ZERO`, `ULP`, `ONE`, `TWO`, … `TEN`, `HUNDRED`, `THOUSAND`,
  `MINUS_ONE`, `HALF`, `TENTH`, `MAX_VALUE`, `MIN_VALUE`
- `static Decimal5f valueOf(long|float|double|BigInteger|BigDecimal|String|Decimal<?>)`,
  each with a `RoundingMode` overload
- `static Decimal5f unscaled(long unscaledValue)`,
  `static Decimal5f unscaled(long unscaledValue, int scale)`

`org.decimal4j.mutable.MutableDecimal5f`
- `MutableDecimal5f()`, and constructors taking
  `long|double|String|BigInteger|BigDecimal|Decimal<?>`
- `static MutableDecimal5f zero()`, `one()`, `two()`, … `ten()`,
  `static MutableDecimal5f unscaled(long unscaledValue)`
- in-place setters: `set(...)`, `setZero()`, `setOne()`, `setMinusOne()`,
  `setUnscaled(long)`, and every arithmetic method mutates and returns `this`.

`org.decimal4j.generic.GenericImmutableDecimal` /
`GenericMutableDecimal` — scale carried at runtime rather than in the type; built
through `GenericDecimalFactory`.

## Arithmetic — `org.decimal4j.api.Decimal`

`add`, `subtract`, `multiply`, `divide`, `remainder`, `negate`, `abs`,
`invert`, `square`, `sqrt`, `pow(int)`, `avg`, `shiftLeft`, `shiftRight`,
`round(int precision)`, each with `RoundingMode` / `TruncationPolicy` overloads
and `…Unscaled(long unscaledValue[, int scale])` and `…Long(long)` variants.

- `Decimal<?> multiplyExact(Decimal<?>)` — widens the scale instead of rounding.
- `Multipliable5f multiplyExact()` — the fluent form: `a.multiplyExact().by(b)`
  returns the exact product at the summed scale (`Multipliable5f.by(Decimal6f)`
  yields a `Decimal11f`). One `Multipliable<N>f` class per scale.
- `<S extends ScaleMetrics> ImmutableDecimal<S> scale(S scaleMetrics)` and
  `scale(int scale[, RoundingMode])` — rescale to a different scale.
- `Decimal<S> multiplyUnscaled(long unscaledMultiplicand, TruncationPolicy)`.
- conversions: `longValue`, `intValue`, `doubleValue`, `floatValue`,
  `toBigDecimal`, `toBigInteger`, `unscaledValue()`, `getScale()`,
  `getScaleMetrics()`, `getFactory()`, `toString()`.

## Scale metrics — `org.decimal4j.scale`

`Scale5f.INSTANCE` (one enum constant per scale) implements `ScaleMetrics`:
- `int getScale()`, `long getScaleFactor()`, `BigInteger getScaleFactorAsBigInteger()`
- `long multiplyByScaleFactor(long)`, `long multiplyByScaleFactorExact(long)`,
  `long mulloByScaleFactor(int)`, `long mulhiByScaleFactor(int)`
- `long divideByScaleFactor(long)`, `long divideUnsignedByScaleFactor(long)`,
  `long moduloByScaleFactor(long)`
- `DecimalArithmetic getDefaultArithmetic()`, `getDefaultCheckedArithmetic()`,
  `getRoundingHalfUpArithmetic()`, `getArithmetic(RoundingMode)`,
  `getCheckedArithmetic(RoundingMode)`, `getArithmetic(TruncationPolicy)`

`org.decimal4j.scale.Scales` — `getScaleMetrics(int scale)`,
`findByScaleFactor(long)`, `VALUES`, `MIN_SCALE`, `MAX_SCALE`.

## Arithmetic back-ends — `org.decimal4j.api.DecimalArithmetic`

Obtained from `ScaleMetrics`; the implementations live in
`org.decimal4j.arithmetic` (`UncheckedScaleNfTruncatingArithmetic`,
`UncheckedScaleNfRoundingArithmetic`, `CheckedScale0fRoundingArithmetic`,
`CheckedScaleNfRoundingArithmetic`, …). All operate on raw unscaled `long`s:
- `int getScale()`, `ScaleMetrics getScaleMetrics()`, `RoundingMode getRoundingMode()`,
  `OverflowMode getOverflowMode()`, `TruncationPolicy getTruncationPolicy()`
- `long add|subtract|multiply|divide|pow|avg|invert|square|sqrt|negate|abs(long …)`
- conversions in: `fromLong(long)`, `fromFloat(float)`, `fromDouble(double)`,
  `fromBigDecimal(BigDecimal)`, `fromBigInteger(BigInteger)`,
  `fromUnscaled(long unscaledValue, int scale)`, `parse(String)`
- conversions out: `toLong`, `toFloat`, `toDouble`, `toBigDecimal`,
  `toUnscaled(long, int scale)`, `toString(long)`
- `DecimalArithmetic deriveArithmetic(RoundingMode|OverflowMode|TruncationPolicy)`

## Factories — `org.decimal4j.factory`

`Factory5f.INSTANCE` implements `DecimalFactory<Scale5f>`:
`getScale()`, `getScaleMetrics()`, `immutableType()`, `mutableType()`,
`valueOf(long|float|double|BigInteger|BigDecimal|String|Decimal<?>)` (with
`RoundingMode` overloads), `valueOfUnscaled(long[, int scale])`,
`newArray(int length)`, `newMutable()`.

`org.decimal4j.factory.Factories` — `getDecimalFactory(int|ScaleMetrics)`,
`getGenericDecimalFactory(int|ScaleMetrics)`, `VALUES`.

`org.decimal4j.generic.GenericDecimalFactory` —
`new GenericDecimalFactory<>(ScaleMetrics)` and the same `valueOf…` API,
returning `GenericImmutableDecimal` / `GenericMutableDecimal`.

## Rounding and overflow — `org.decimal4j.truncate`

- `DecimalRounding` — enum mirroring `RoundingMode`
  (`UP`, `DOWN`, `CEILING`, `FLOOR`, `HALF_UP`, `HALF_DOWN`, `HALF_EVEN`,
  `UNNECESSARY`); `getRoundingMode()`,
  `int calculateRoundingIncrement(int sign, long truncatedValue, TruncatedPart)`,
  `static DecimalRounding valueOf(RoundingMode)`.
- `TruncatedPart` — `ZERO`, `LESS_THAN_HALF_BUT_NOT_ZERO`, `EQUAL_TO_HALF`,
  `GREATER_THAN_HALF`; `boolean isGreaterThanZero()`,
  `boolean isGreaterEqualHalf()`,
  `static TruncatedPart valueOf(int firstTruncatedDigit, boolean zeroAfter)`.
- `OverflowMode` — `UNCHECKED`, `CHECKED`; `boolean isChecked()`.
- `TruncationPolicy`, and the two enums implementing it: `UncheckedRounding`
  (`toCheckedRounding()`) and `CheckedRounding` (`toUncheckedRounding()`), each
  with a constant per rounding mode and `static … valueOf(RoundingMode)`.

## Utilities — `org.decimal4j.util`

`DoubleRounder` — `new DoubleRounder(int precision)`,
`new DoubleRounder(ScaleMetrics)`, `int getPrecision()`,
`double round(double[, RoundingMode])`, and the statics
`DoubleRounder.round(double value, int precision[, RoundingMode])`.

	 * fraction.

	 * The fraction consists of a decimal point followed by zero or more decimal
	 * digits. The string must contain at least one digit in either the integer
	 * or the fraction. If the fraction contains more than 2 digits, the

	 * exception is thrown if the value is too large to be represented as a

package bench.generated;

import org.openjdk.jmh.annotations.*;

import java.math.BigDecimal;
import java.math.BigInteger;

@BenchmarkMode(Mode.AverageTime)
@OutputTimeUnit(TimeUnit.NANOSECONDS)
@Fork(1)
@Warmup(iterations = 1, time = 1)
@Measurement(iterations = 3, time = 1)
public class MutableDecimal2fBenchmark {

    @State(Scope.Thread)
    public static class ThreadState {
        private static final int SIZE = 1024; // power of two for fast modulo

        MutableDecimal2f[] receivers;
        MutableDecimal2f[] operands;
        long[] longValues;
        double[] doubleValues;
        int index = 0;

        @Setup(Level.Trial)

            receivers = new MutableDecimal2f[SIZE];
            operands = new MutableDecimal2f[SIZE];
            longValues = new long[SIZE];
            doubleValues = new double[SIZE];

                longValues[i] = 12345L;
                doubleValues[i] = 123.456;
            }

        public int nextIndex() {
            int i = index;
            index = (index + 1) & (SIZE - 1);
            return i;
        }
    }
